# `silk/i16`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Sixteen-bit signed integers with explicit overflow, conversion, and text policies.

## When to use

Use `i16` for data whose public representation is exactly sixteen signed bits, such as a binary
field or compact sample. Use `i32` or `i64` when the range is not itself part of the contract.

## Details

Ordinary arithmetic, narrowing conversions, division by zero, and invalid shift counts trap.
Choose `checked*` to receive [`Option`](./option.md#declaration-73696c6b2f6f7074696f6e3a3a4f7074696f6e) on invalid arithmetic, `wrapping*` for arithmetic modulo
2^16, or `saturating*` to clamp at [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d494e) and [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d4158). Signed right shifts preserve the sign bit.

Decimal [`parse`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a7061727365) requires a complete, in-range representation. Use [`Format`](./format.md#declaration-73696c6b2f666f726d61743a3a466f726d6174) with
`Format.display` for defaults or `Format.displayWith` for explicit options. Both operations
stream through a mutable `Writer` without `Allocator`.

## Gotchas

[`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d494e) cannot be represented as a positive i16, so ordinary [`negate`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a6e6567617465) traps for that value.

## Examples

### Preserve the sign during a right shift

```silk
import silk.i16

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let shifted = i16.shiftRight(-84, 1)
  return i16.toI32(i16.negate(shifted))
}
```

Import as `i16` with `import silk.i16`.

Public declarations: 59.

## `negate`

```silk
pub fn negate(value: i16) -> i16
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value` and traps when `value` is [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d494e). Use
this function when that boundary is a program error.

<a id="declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a7772617070696e674e6567617465"></a>

## `wrappingNegate`

```silk
pub fn wrappingNegate(value: i16) -> i16
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value`, wrapped to the `i16` range. [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d494e)
stays [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d494e). Use this function for deliberate modulo arithmetic.

<a id="declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a73617475726174696e674e6567617465"></a>

## `saturatingNegate`

```silk
pub fn saturatingNegate(value: i16) -> i16
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value`, clamped to the `i16` range. [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d494e)
becomes [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6931363a3a4d4158). Use this function when the positive boundary is required.

## `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> silk/result.Result<i16, silk/format.ParseError>
```

Reads the complete text as a signed decimal `i16`.

### Details

A failure contains `silk.format.NotANumber` for empty text, a leading `+`, a non-digit, or
trailing bytes. It contains `silk.format.OutOfRange` if the number is outside the `i16` range.
